notes: English version of middle.json: same ids, same option order (correct/funny indexes come from the RU file).
Adapted, not literal: Yandex Metrica → Google Analytics, Webvisor → session recording, Russian acronyms in joke options → English ones.

questions.question: We watch people do tasks in the product and look for where they stumble. This is…
questions.explanation: The core usability method: we watch behavior instead of asking for opinions.

questions.question: A one-on-one conversation with a user about their experience and tasks is…
questions.explanation: An interview answers “why”, a survey answers “how many”.

questions.question: “If we simplify the form, sign-ups will grow” — this is a…
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is phrased so that it can be tested.

questions.question: A non-obvious finding about people's behavior from research is an…
questions.explanation: An insight explains why people act the way they do.

questions.question: A composite portrait of a typical user with goals and pains is a…
questions.explanation: A persona helps the team remember who the product is for.

questions.question: A diagram of all site pages and how they nest inside each other is a…
questions.explanation: A sitemap shows structure; a user flow shows the path to a goal.

questions.question: A collection of images to capture the mood and style of a future design is a…
questions.explanation: Agree on the moodboard before mockups so you don't argue about taste later.

questions.question: A screen layout of blocks and labels, with no colors or images, is a…
questions.explanation: A wireframe locks in structure and content priorities.

questions.question: A static design that looks like the finished product but isn't clickable is a…
questions.explanation: You can click through a prototype, not a mockup.

questions.question: A prototype that looks just like the finished product is…
questions.explanation: High fidelity means high detail: colors, copy, animations.

questions.question: Components, rules and styles used to build the whole product are a…
questions.explanation: A UI kit is a set of parts; a design system is parts plus rules and processes.

questions.question: A document with rules on how to use the product's elements and style is a…
questions.explanation: Material Design and Apple HIG, for example, are platform guidelines.

questions.question: A document with the client's task, filled in before work starts, is a…
questions.explanation: A brief covers goals, audience, deadlines, constraints and examples.

questions.question: An expert checks an interface against a list of principles, no users. Method:
questions.explanation: Most often it's checked against Nielsen's 10 heuristics.

questions.question: The more menu items, the longer it takes to choose. Whose law is it?
questions.explanation: Decision time grows with the number of options.

questions.question: By Miller's law, how many items can a person hold in memory at once?
questions.explanation: That's why long lists and numbers are broken into chunks.

questions.question: How well a product works for people with visual, hearing or motor impairments is…
questions.explanation: Often shortened to a11y.

questions.question: The difference in lightness between text and background that affects readability is…
questions.explanation: The WCAG AA minimum for normal text is 4.5:1.

questions.question: The outline around a button when you reach it with the Tab key shows…
questions.explanation: Without a visible focus, the interface can't be used with a keyboard.

questions.question: Short interface texts — on buttons, in hints, in errors — are…
questions.explanation: Microcopy is the UX writer's turf.

questions.question: The consistent character and manner in which a product “talks” is its…
questions.explanation: Tone of voice: friendly, strict, ironic…

questions.question: Color shows where people click most on a page. What's this map called?
questions.explanation: A heatmap shows clicks, cursor movement or scroll depth.

questions.question: Hotjar's feature that replays a visitor's actions like a video is…
questions.explanation: It helps you see where people get stuck on a page.

questions.question: Text above a form field that says what to enter is a…
questions.explanation: Unlike a placeholder, a label doesn't disappear while typing.

questions.question: Checking whether a form field is filled in correctly is…
questions.explanation: Better to check a field right after input, not after the whole form is submitted.

questions.question: Checking that you are you (login and password) is called…
questions.explanation: Authorization is the next step: what you're allowed to do.

questions.question: The “prove you're not a robot” task is a…
questions.explanation: CAPTCHA stops bots but annoys people and can be inaccessible.

questions.question: A message an app sends to the phone's screen is a…
questions.explanation: Push notifications bring users back but quickly get annoying.

questions.question: A user's problems and irritations along their path are…
questions.explanation: Pain points are found in interviews and marked on the CJM.

questions.question: Any place where a customer meets the product or company is a…
questions.explanation: Touchpoints: website, email, support call, packaging.

questions.question: Passing finished designs and specs to developers is…
questions.explanation: A good handoff: mockups, states, spacing and answers to questions.

questions.question: Quick hand drawings to find an idea for a solution are…
questions.explanation: Sketches are cheap: you don't mind throwing them away.

questions.question: A one-page site for a single goal — sell, book, collect leads — is a…
questions.explanation: A landing page is where traffic “lands”.

questions.question: A user arrived on a page and left right away. What's this called?
questions.explanation: The share of such visits is the bounce rate.

questions.question: A scenario where something goes wrong — no network, failed payment — is the…
questions.explanation: Unhappy paths are designed on par with the main one.

questions.question: A user spends long sessions in the product and comes back regularly. This is…
questions.explanation: Engagement is measured by frequency, duration and depth of use.

questions.question: Google's service that counts site visits, traffic sources and goals:
questions.explanation: Web analytics: visits, bounces, goal conversions.

questions.question: The “Frequently asked questions” block on a site is abbreviated as…
questions.explanation: Frequently Asked Questions.

questions.question: A team throws out as many ideas as possible in an hour, without criticism. This is…
questions.explanation: Criticism waits, so ideas don't get killed early.

questions.question: What's a survey question answered in your own words called?
questions.explanation: Closed means picking from options; a rating scale means scoring on a scale.

questions.question: The Figma feature that lines up elements in a row or column with spacing:
questions.explanation: Auto layout is like flexbox in code.

questions.question: A copy of a main component placed in a Figma design is an…
questions.explanation: An instance updates when the main component changes.

questions.question: All states of a button inside one Figma component are…
questions.explanation: Variants switch via properties: size, state, type.

questions.question: Saved colors, fonts and shadows for reuse in Figma are…
questions.explanation: Change a style and every element using it updates.

questions.question: An extension that adds new features to Figma is a…
questions.explanation: Plugins are installed from Figma Community.

questions.question: The main container for a screen in Figma is a…
questions.explanation: A frame supports auto layout, grids and clipping; a group doesn't.

questions.question: Hiding part of an image by the shape of another layer in Figma is a…
questions.explanation: The bottom layer sets the shape; layers above show only inside it.

questions.question: Column guides laid over a frame in Figma are a…
questions.explanation: The grid is set up in the frame's right panel.

questions.question: In Auto layout, how do you stretch a field to the parent's full width?
questions.explanation: Fill takes all the space, Hug wraps the content, Fixed keeps its own size.

questions.question: To get an icon out of Figma as SVG, you use the section…
questions.explanation: In Export you pick the format: PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF.

questions.question: Two fonts together, one for headings and one for body text, are a…
questions.explanation: A classic: sans-serif headings with serif body text, or the other way round.

questions.question: Regular, Bold and Italic of one font are different…
questions.explanation: A typeface is the family; a style is a variant inside it.

questions.question: What do typographers call font size?
questions.explanation: On the web, it's set with font-size.

questions.question: Small strokes at the ends of letters are…
questions.explanation: Fonts with them are serif; without them, sans-serif.

questions.question: Text aligned to both the left and right edges is…
questions.explanation: Justified text is rare on the web: it creates “rivers” of spaces.

questions.question: A limited set of colors an interface is built from is a…
questions.explanation: Usually: primary, accent, neutrals and status colors.

questions.question: A smooth transition from one color to another is a…
questions.explanation: It can be linear, radial or angular.

questions.question: A bright color for the main button and the most important elements is…
questions.explanation: Accents work when there are few of them.

questions.question: Which Figma property sets a layer's transparency?
questions.explanation: Transparency can be set for the layer and separately for the fill.

questions.question: The Drop shadow effect in Figma is…
questions.explanation: Inner shadow is a shadow inside the shape.

questions.question: How do you blur what's under a translucent panel in Figma?
questions.explanation: Layer blur blurs the layer itself; background blur blurs what's below.

questions.question: Icons drawn with a single stroke and no fill are called…
questions.explanation: Outline and filled are the two main icon styles.

questions.question: The build matches the design down to the pixel. This is…
questions.explanation: A requirement for how precisely a design is turned into code.

questions.question: The screen width at which the layout changes is a…
questions.explanation: Breakpoints are set in CSS media queries.

questions.question: The gap between grid columns is called the…
questions.explanation: Margins are the space from the edge; gutters are the gaps between columns.

questions.question: An element's outer spacing from its neighbors is…
questions.explanation: Padding is inner spacing, margin is outer.

questions.question: What's the outline of a shape called in Figma?
questions.explanation: A stroke has a weight and a position: inside, outside or center.

questions.question: Which color is #00FF00?
questions.explanation: Two characters per channel: red 00, green FF, blue 00.

questions.question: Light text on a dark background across the whole interface is a…
questions.explanation: A dark theme is designed separately, not by simply inverting colors.

questions.question: The button was tapped and the request is still running. Which state to show?
questions.explanation: A spinner on the button protects against a second tap.

questions.question: What is the state of a button at the moment it's pressed called?
questions.explanation: Main states: default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled.

questions.question: You need to pick several options from a list. Which control fits?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons are for one option out of several.

questions.question: A handle used to pick a value from a range is a…
questions.explanation: A slider is good when the exact value isn't critical.

questions.question: A “1 — 2 — 3” bar above a checkout form showing the steps is a…
questions.explanation: It shows how many steps are left.

questions.question: A little circle with the unread count on an icon is a…
questions.explanation: A badge draws attention to what's new.

questions.question: An icon of three vertical dots that opens a menu is a…
questions.explanation: Three horizontal lines are a hamburger; three dots in a column are a kebab.

questions.question: Blocks that expand and collapse when you click their heading are an…
questions.explanation: Good for FAQs and long settings.

questions.question: Switches between sections within one area of the screen are…
questions.explanation: Tabs show one section at a time.

questions.question: A block where slides change with arrows or a swipe is a…
questions.explanation: Few people ever reach the last slides of a carousel.

questions.question: A long list split into numbered pages at the bottom is…
questions.explanation: Alternatives: “Show more” and infinite scroll.

questions.question: A minimal version of a product to quickly test an idea with people is an…
questions.explanation: Minimum Viable Product — a concept from Lean Startup.

questions.question: The path from visit to purchase where some people drop off at each step is a…
questions.explanation: Funnel analysis shows at which step we lose people.

questions.question: The share of users who come back to the product a few days later is…
questions.explanation: Retention is the main sign that the product is needed.

questions.question: The number of unique users per month is the metric…
questions.explanation: DAU — per day, WAU — per week, MAU — per month.

questions.question: The share of clicks out of a banner's or link's impressions is the metric…
questions.explanation: Click-Through Rate = clicks / impressions.

questions.question: “How likely are you to recommend us to a friend?” — the metric…
questions.explanation: Net Promoter Score — an index of willingness to recommend.

questions.question: A plan for the product's development by stages and dates is a…
questions.explanation: A backlog is a list of tasks; a roadmap is their plan over time.

questions.question: Shipping a new version of the product to users is a…
questions.explanation: Before a release — testing; after — collecting feedback.

questions.question: A single product function in team slang is a…
questions.explanation: “It's not a bug, it's a feature” — a classic.

questions.question: A defect in how a program works is a…
questions.explanation: Engineers called glitches “bugs” as far back as Edison, in the 1870s.

questions.question: Who in Scrum makes sure the team follows the process?
questions.explanation: The Product Owner owns the backlog; the Scrum Master owns the process.

questions.question: An end-of-sprint meeting where the team shows what it built is a…
questions.explanation: In the Scrum Guide it's the Sprint Review.

questions.question: A key performance indicator is abbreviated as…
questions.explanation: Key Performance Indicator.

questions.question: What sets a product apart from all its competitors is its…
questions.explanation: Unique Selling Proposition.

questions.question: Reviewing rival products — what they do, cost and look like — is…
questions.explanation: It helps you find how to stand out.

questions.question: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats — this is a… analysis
questions.explanation: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats.

questions.question: The way a product makes money is…
questions.explanation: Subscription, ads, one-time purchases, commission…

questions.question: The basic version is free, the advanced one is paid. This model is…
questions.explanation: Freemium = free + premium.

questions.question: The role of the person responsible for developing the product as a whole is…
questions.explanation: The product manager decides what to build and why; the team decides how.

questions.question: A set of paid plans “Basic / Pro / Business” on one page is…
questions.explanation: Plans are compared in a table, with the recommended one highlighted.

questions.question: Nielsen: on the web, people don't read text, they…
questions.explanation: That's why headings, lists and highlights matter.

questions.question: What do designers call dummy text in a mockup?
questions.explanation: Dummy text is later replaced with real copy — and the layout often falls apart.

questions.question: Which shortcut creates a component in Figma (Windows)?
questions.explanation: On Mac it's Option+Cmd+K.

questions.question: A Figma component property to swap an icon right in an instance:
questions.explanation: No need to detach the instance.

questions.question: Light and dark themes in one Variables collection are different…
questions.explanation: A frame switches between modes in one click.

questions.question: What's the container with all variants of a component called in Figma?
questions.explanation: It's outlined with a purple dashed border.

questions.question: Unlinking an instance from its main component in Figma is…
questions.explanation: After detaching, the instance becomes a regular frame.

questions.question: Changes in an instance that don't touch the main component are…
questions.explanation: For example, different text on a button.

questions.question: A Figma prototype transition that smoothly moves matching layers by itself:
questions.explanation: Layers must have the same names on both screens.

questions.question: All links are blue and underlined, so we see them as a group. Principle of…
questions.explanation: Elements that look alike seem related.

questions.question: A card's border groups everything inside it. Principle of…
questions.explanation: Elements within a shared boundary are perceived as a group.

questions.question: Card sorting where participants name the groups themselves is called…
questions.explanation: In closed sorting, the groups are set in advance.

questions.question: A good error message says what happened and…
questions.explanation: Without a hint on what to do, an error is a dead end.

questions.question: An animation speeds up smoothly and slows down smoothly. This curve is…
questions.explanation: Ease-in is a slow start, ease-out a slow finish.

questions.question: Which Figma property changes the spacing between all letters?
questions.explanation: Line height is between lines; paragraph spacing is between paragraphs.

questions.question: The Figma tool to pick a color from anywhere on the screen:
questions.explanation: The shortcut is I.

questions.question: What WCAG AA contrast is enough for large text?
questions.explanation: Large means 18 pt and up, or 14 pt bold.

questions.question: Default, hover, pressed, focus and… Which button state is missing?
questions.explanation: Disabled — the action isn't available right now.

questions.question: Minimum tap target per Material Design:
questions.explanation: The icon can be smaller, the touch area can't.

questions.question: Atomic Design: atoms → molecules → … → templates → pages. What's missing?
questions.explanation: An organism is a complex block of molecules, like a site header.

questions.question: Named color and spacing values shared by the design and code are…
questions.explanation: For example, color-primary or space-16.

questions.question: A user's idea of how a system works is their…
questions.explanation: It's convenient when the interface matches that idea.

questions.question: Rare settings are hidden under “Advanced”. This technique is called…
questions.explanation: The essentials first, the complex stuff on demand.

questions.question: A button looks like it can be pressed. This property is called…
questions.explanation: Affordance hints at what action is possible.

questions.question: The “two diamonds” model: explore → narrow → find solutions → choose:
questions.explanation: A model by the UK Design Council.

questions.question: How much mental effort it takes to figure out an interface is…
questions.explanation: Extra elements and decisions raise the load.

questions.question: 5551234567 is easier to read as (555) 123-4567. This technique is…
questions.explanation: Breaking information into meaningful pieces.

questions.question: “Profile 60% complete” bugs you until you finish it. This is the… effect
questions.explanation: Unfinished things are remembered better than finished ones.

questions.question: A dropdown list with a search field right inside is a…
questions.explanation: Handy when there are dozens of options.

questions.question: A participant takes the test alone, following instructions, no moderator. Test:
questions.explanation: Cheaper and faster, but you can't ask “why”.

questions.question: “You liked the new button, didn't you?” What's wrong with this question?
questions.explanation: It suggests the “right” answer and skews the data.

questions.question: The team estimates tasks with Fibonacci number cards. This is…
questions.explanation: Everyone reveals their cards at once so they don't sway each other.

questions.question: A start-of-sprint meeting where the team decides what it will do is…
questions.explanation: In Scrum it's Sprint Planning.

questions.question: Creating a new market with no competitors yet is the… strategy
questions.explanation: In a “red ocean”, companies fight over existing demand.

questions.question: A small window that opens on click next to an element, with buttons or a form:
questions.explanation: A tooltip is just text on hover; a popover is interactive.
